html:
The Ngwato, or Bamangwato, are the largest of the Tswana chiefdoms of what is now Botswana. The map shows their land in 1880 and 1900, when it was the strongest African state between the Boer republics and the Zambezi.

Their most famous ruler, Khama III, reigned from 1875 to 1923. A devout Christian, he banned alcohol and moved his capital from Shoshong to Palapye in 1889 and to Serowe in 1902. Threatened by the Boers of the Transvaal and by the Ndebele to the north, he welcomed British protection, and the Bechuanaland Protectorate was declared in 1885.

When Cecil Rhodes wanted his British South Africa Company to take over the protectorate, Khama and two other chiefs travelled to London in 1895 and persuaded the government to refuse. That kept Botswana out of white settler rule. Khama's grandson Seretse Khama became the country's first president in 1966.
